idiom_name: Process::Sys.setresuid / setresgid drop plus Forwardable delegation for a narrowed view
implementation_notes: Ruby has the syscall bindings - Process::Sys.setresuid, setresgid, seteuid and setreuid, documented as direct bindings to the same-named calls and as not available on all platforms - and Process.setrlimit for resource limits, but no authority model: taint tracking was removed in Ruby 3.0, where the release notes state that the $SAFE feature became a normal global variable, so nothing in the interpreter tracks trusted data any more. What replaces a rights table in-process is delegation: Forwardable's def_delegators, or DelegateClass, expose only the methods a collaborator needs, so authority is narrowed by the object you pass rather than by a check you remember to call. The classic policy-object form (CanCan abilities, Pundit policies) remains justified inside a request, where authority is business data; the operating-system identity of the process is still the only boundary that holds against code you do not trust.
code_sketch:
require 'forwardable'

class ReadOnlyRepo
  extend Forwardable
  def_delegators :@repo, :find, :all          # write methods are not exposed
  def initialize(repo) = @repo = repo
end

Process::Sys.setresuid(-1, uid, uid)          # drop before handling input
Process::Sys.setresgid(-1, gid, gid)
pitfalls: Taint tracking is gone: Ruby 3.0 removed $SAFE and the taint mechanism entirely, so any code whose least-privilege story depended on trusted or untrusted data marks now has no runtime enforcement at that layer.

Forwardable and private/protected narrow the API, not the object: a delegator that hands back the underlying object, or a method that returns it, gives the authority straight back, and send/public_send, instance_variable_get, eval and ObjectSpace go around visibility.

Process::Sys calls are documented as not available on all platforms and raise SystemCallError on failure, so a rescue that swallows the error leaves the process at its original privilege - check that the drop happened rather than assuming it did.
